findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the hand sink to the left of the triple sink to be damaged. The faucet was detached from the sink and lying in the sink basin. The PIC was aware of the damage and has requested repair. Inspectors will follow-up at the facility on November 23, 2026 to ensure the sink has been repaired. Please contact the Department if repairs cannot be completed in the requested time.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a mop to be stored directly in the sink basin. This storage method does not allow for required drip-drying of the mop head. The PIC was informed and relocated the mop. Ensure the mop is stored in a manner that allows drip-drying to occur to prevent microbial growth.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a tile to be damaged to the left of the mop sink. This tile seals the wall to the flooring of the kitchen space. Ensure this tile is repaired or replaced to prevent pest movement or microbial growth behind the tiles or inside the wall.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: No certified food protection manager (CFM) is present at the facility. There should be a CFM present at all times food or drinks are being served. Inspector provided a list of accredited providers to the person in charge (PIC). Ensure there is at least one CFM is present at all times the facility is operating.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the basin of the kitchen hand-sink to be obstructed by a cardboard box at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- the cardboard box was removed from the hand-sink basin. Hand-washing sinks should be stocked and accessible at all times to allow for proper hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: During the start of the inspection the sanitizer buckets were observed to have a concentration of 0 ppm quaternary ammonia, and the sanitizer at the triple sink contained 50 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- food handler remade sanitizer buckets and sanitizer water at the triple sink to be within the desired concentration (200-400 ppm). Ensure sanitizer is changed at a frequency to obtain the required concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Two gallons of milk in the counter cooler were observed to not contain any date marking. When the inspector asked the person in charge (PIC) when the milk was opened, they stated it was opened yesterday. CORRECTED-PIC placed a date on both containers of milk. Ensure that items that are not used within the day of service are marked with the date they were first opened, and used or discarded within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Debris and soil accumulation were observed around the dishwasher and under the ice machine in the kitchen. Clean under and around equipment in the cafe.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There was no certified food protection manager present during this visit, despite food service occurring. Ensure sufficient staff are CFMs to cover all shifts of food prep and service. Keep CFM certificates on file for review during inspections.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: There were no signed reporting agreement on file for the two employees working during this inspection. Inspector emailed the form to PIC. Print reporting agreements and have employees review and sign. Keep signed reporting agreements on file for all employees.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
One of the facility’s probe thermometers read 30F at room temperature. When placed in ice water, the thermometer read below zero. CORRECTED- The thermometer was calibrated using the ice water method. 
4-203.11: (A) FOOD TEMP. MEASURING DEVICE shall be accurate to  +/- 1 Celsius (B) accurate to +/- 2 Fahrenheit. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Facility does not have quat test strips available to check sanitizer concentration. Ensure appropriate test strips are available and readily accessible for the sanitizer in use.
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Debris and soil accumulation observed around the dishwasher and under the ice machine. Clean under and around equipment throughout the cafe.
2) Debris accumulation observed under the back dry storage shelves and back storage coolers/freezers. Sweep regularly to prevent accumulation.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Food handler certificates were not available for the two employees present during this inspection. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed. Keep food handler certificates available for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  [C]
